title: One task per loop iteration, with a fresh context each time
statement: In an autonomous build loop, do exactly one task per iteration and spawn a fresh instance each time, keeping per-iteration context as small as possible, because output quality falls as the window fills.
rationale: A single monolithic process doing one thing per loop avoids the non-determinism of many chattering agents, and a fresh window each iteration sidesteps context rot. Memory persists on disk between iterations, not in a growing window.
applies_when: Running a Ralph-style or factory-style unattended loop
Tasks can be decomposed into small independently-completable units
not_when: A single interactive session where the human is steering turn by turn
how: Scope each task to well under the usable context window
Persist plan and progress to files so a fresh instance can resume
Narrow back to strictly one item per loop the moment output degrades
check: Does each iteration start a fresh instance and complete one scoped task, with state carried on disk rather than in a growing context? If iterations share a ballooning window, this is violated.
failure_if_absent: Iterations accumulate context, quality clips at the window limit, and the loop produces progressively worse code.
